paper_title: Transactional Shared Memory for Multiagent Systems via Policy-Consistent Commit and Provenance-Driven Repair
scope: Paper-focused source and experiment snapshots, not a full server/disk backup.
excluded_categories: Unrelated CQ electricity-market experiments and outputs
Installed virtual environments, caches and compiled Python bytecode
Model weights (already excluded by the server export)
Git object databases and binary transfer bundles; source snapshots are included
Repeated development checkouts not selected as a named snapshot
Privileged controller private records, signing/authorization material and unrelated failure diagnostics
Vendored third-party dependency installations under external_data/deps; acquisition scripts and manifests are retained
LongMemEval runtime data, which is not a reported experiment in this submission
The original compressed archives remain local; selected contents are stored as individual files
Downloaded G-Memory/A-MEM source copies; pinned fetch script and per-file hashes are retained, following the supplied campaign reproduction instructions.
limitations: Some public-runtime reports explicitly state raw_reports_committed=false; this backup does not assert those absent traces were recovered.
Symbolic links are not dereferenced. Selected source/data snapshots use regular files only.
Historical and pilot results are preserved separately and are not evidence for final paper claims.
The supplied PDF is identified by SHA256; the manuscript itself is not uploaded.

The final multi_agent_controlled_v1/data directory was not found in the three server archives; the generator, final CSV results, and reproducibility hashes are retained from the existing GitHub commit.
The v10 performance package contains aggregate measurements, not all 14,400 per-operation raw samples.
